events.title: Battle of Lake Erie
events.description: During the War of 1812, a U.S. Navy squadron commanded by Oliver Hazard Perry defeated and captured an entire British Royal Navy squadron on Lake Erie near Put-in-Bay, Ohio. Perry reported, 'We have met the enemy and they are ours.'
events.significance: The victory gave the United States control of Lake Erie, forced British withdrawal from Detroit, and paved the way for the American victory at the Battle of the Thames.

events.title: Treaty of Saint-Germain-en-Laye Signed
events.description: The Allied Powers and Austria signed the Treaty of Saint-Germain-en-Laye, formally dissolving the Austro-Hungarian Empire and recognizing Austria as a small republic.
events.significance: The treaty redrew the map of Central Europe, recognized new states such as Czechoslovakia and Yugoslavia, and prohibited union (Anschluss) between Austria and Germany.

events.title: Canada Declares War on Germany
events.description: One week after Britain and France, Canada declared war on Nazi Germany, following a parliamentary vote under Prime Minister William Lyon Mackenzie King, with King George VI giving royal assent as King of Canada.
events.significance: It marked Canada's independent entry into World War II as a sovereign nation, demonstrating its autonomy within the British Commonwealth.

events.title: Assassination of Empress Elisabeth of Austria
events.description: Empress Elisabeth ('Sisi') of Austria, wife of Emperor Franz Joseph I, was stabbed by Italian anarchist Luigi Lucheni on the shore of Lake Geneva in Switzerland and died shortly afterward.
events.significance: Her death shocked Europe, intensified crackdowns on anarchist movements, and was a further personal tragedy for the Habsburg dynasty in the years before World War I.

events.title: Switzerland Joins the United Nations
events.description: Switzerland became the 190th member of the United Nations after a 2002 referendum in which Swiss voters narrowly approved membership.
events.significance: It ended Switzerland's long tradition of staying outside the UN and marked a notable shift in Swiss foreign policy while retaining its neutrality.
